note: Reading list for the self-study law curriculum. Each book carries a `verified` field: 'confirmed' means edition/publisher details were checked against a publisher or bookseller listing; 'unconfirmed' means the title is right but the current edition was NOT checked — verify before purchase. Malaysian legal textbooks go stale fast; always pair a textbook with the current statute text from AGC.

verificationLevels.confirmed: Edition, publisher and/or ISBN checked against a publisher or specialist bookseller listing.
verificationLevels.unconfirmed: Title and author believed correct; current edition NOT verified. Check before buying.

roles.primary: Main text for the module. Read cover to cover.
roles.reference: Consult for specific points. Do not read linearly.
roles.method: Teaches how to study/read/reason, not doctrine.

books.title: Glanville Williams: Learning the Law
books.author: Glanville Williams
books.notes: Covers reading statutes and case law, solving legal problems, study methods, exam prep, legal research. English legal system framing, but the method transfers to Malaysia. Highest-priority purchase.

books.title: Letters to a Law Student
books.author: Nicholas J. McBride
books.notes: Informal guide to reading, arguing and structuring legal answers. Good motivational entry point.

books.title: Reading Like a Lawyer: Time-Saving Strategies for Reading Law Like an Expert
books.author: Ruth Ann McKinney
books.notes: Directly addresses the novice/expert legal reading gap identified in the research (Deegan; Christensen). Read early and re-read.

books.title: Thinking Like a Lawyer: A New Introduction to Legal Reasoning
books.author: Frederick Schauer
books.notes: Precedent, analogy, authority, rules. Read AFTER briefing several cases, not before.

books.title: The Rule of Law
books.author: Tom Bingham
books.notes: Short, plain-language entry into public law thinking. Cheap.

books.title: Make It Stick: The Science of Successful Learning
books.author: Peter C. Brown, Henry L. Roediger III, Mark A. McDaniel
books.notes: Retrieval practice and spacing evidence in readable form. Read before building any flashcards.

books.title: Malaysian Legal System
books.author: Various contributors
books.notes: 36 chapters, multi-author, incorporating recent updates on the Malaysian legal system. More current than Wu Min Aun.

books.title: The Malaysian Legal System
books.author: Wu Min Aun
books.notes: Still the most-cited student text on Malaysian LLB reading lists, but 20 years old. Use for structure and legal history only. DO NOT rely on it for current law.

books.title: A First Look at the Malaysian Legal System
books.author: Wan Arfah Hamzah
books.notes: Gentler entry point than Wu or Ashgar. Verify current edition.

books.title: Our Constitution
books.author: Shad Saleem Faruqi
books.notes: 9 parts, 36 chapters: characteristics of the Federal Constitution, separation of powers, fundamental liberties, citizenship, Conference of Rulers, Yang di-Pertuan Agong, ministerial responsibility, making of laws, judiciary, electoral process, powers to combat subversion. Written for the general reader — ideal starting point.

books.title: Document of Destiny: The Constitution of the Federation of Malaysia
books.author: Shad Saleem Faruqi
books.notes: The deep treatment. Buy after Our Constitution. Author was reported to be updating this — check for a newer edition.

books.title: Criminal Law in Malaysia and Singapore
books.author: Stanley Yeo, Neil Morgan, Chan Wing Cheong
books.notes: Leading academic treatment of the Penal Code. VERIFY CURRENT EDITION — must post-date the Abolition of Mandatory Death Penalty Act 2023.

books.title: Janab's Key to Criminal Procedure
books.author: Hamid Sultan bin Abu Backer
books.editor: Mah Weng Kwai, Ravinthran Paramaguru (revising editors)
books.notes: Two parts: criminal procedure in 70 sub-chapters, plus commentary on all 445 CPC sections. Includes MY/SG/India comparison chart. Updated only to Q3 2018 — does NOT include the 2023 death-penalty reforms. Verify all sentencing separately.

books.title: Contract Law in Malaysia
books.author: Cheong May Fong, Choong Shaw Mei, Yong Kai Jie
books.notes: Most current major Malaysian doctrinal text available. Covers the full contract life cycle: formation, terms, voidable contracts, void agreements, discharge, remedies. Case law updated from 2010 onwards with Federal Court decisions. ASK FOR THE STUDENT EDITION — substantially cheaper.

books.title: The Law of Contract
books.author: Visu Sinnadurai
books.notes: The leading Malaysian contract treatise; first port of call for students, practitioners and judges. Reference work, not a first read. Companion: Contracts Act: A Commentary (2015).

books.title: Norchaya Talib on Torts in Malaysia
books.author: Norchaya Talib (original)
books.notes: Negligence, nuisance, trespass, strict liability, defamation. New material: tort of harassment, defence of illegality, exclusion clauses, damages, developments in defamation, extension of vicarious liability. Student Edition available.

books.title: Land Law in Malaysia: Cases and Commentary
books.author: Teo Keang Sood, Khaw Lake Tee
books.notes: VERIFY CURRENT EDITION before buying.

books.title: Malaysian Torrens System
books.author: Salleh Buang
books.notes: VERIFY CURRENT EDITION.

books.title: Companies Act of Malaysia: An Annotation (Desk Edition)
books.notes: Seen listed as a current annotation by Malaysian law booksellers; publisher and author details need checking. NOTE: Walter Woon on Company Law is SINGAPORE law — do not substitute it.

books.title: Malaysian Law of Evidence (Student Edition)
books.notes: Case law updated to July 2023. Covers documentary evidence in depth, child witnesses including the 2023 amendments to the Evidence of Child Witness Act 2007 and the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017. Most current student evidence option found. Author/edition details need confirming with the bookseller.

books.title: Law of Evidence in Malaysia
books.author: Mazlina Mahali
books.notes: Explicitly aimed at undergraduates and CLP candidates. Explains differences between common law and the Malaysian position under the Evidence Act 1950.

books.title: Sarkar's Law of Evidence (Second Malaysia Edition)
books.author: Sarkar
books.notes: Places the Evidence Act 1950 within Sarkar's scheme; Malaysian provisions and commentary follow the corresponding Indian sections. Updated to August 2019. Expensive 3-volume reference — skip unless going deep.

books.title: Janab's Key to Civil Procedure
books.author: Hamid Sultan bin Abu Backer
books.editor: Mah Weng Kwai, Arun Kasi (revising editors)
books.notes: Readable introduction to civil procedure. Updated to Q3 2018 — check Rules of Court amendments since.

books.title: Malaysian Civil Procedure (the 'White Book')
books.notes: The practitioner's authoritative annotation of the Rules of Court 2012. Published annually. Expensive — buy the current year only if budget allows.

books.title: Administrative Law
books.author: William Wade, Christopher Forsyth
books.notes: INTERIM SUBSTITUTE. No dominant current Malaysian student text on administrative law was found. Use an English text for principles (legality, procedural fairness, natural justice, legitimate expectation, reasonableness, ultra vires) and read Malaysian judicial review judgments directly for the local position. Flagged gap — revisit.

statutes.title: Federal Constitution of Malaysia
statutes.notes: Also available as a printed reprint from PNMB/ILBS — worth buying for annotation.

statutes.title: Contracts Act 1950
statutes.notes: In pari materia with the Indian Contract Act 1872. Read section by section alongside Cheong.

statutes.title: Penal Code
statutes.notes: Amended by the Abolition of Mandatory Death Penalty Act 2023 (Act 846), effective 4 July 2023.

statutes.title: Evidence Act 1950
statutes.notes: 3 Parts, 11 chapters, 167 sections. Part I Relevancy, Part II Proof, Part III Production and Effect of Evidence.

statutes.title: National Land Code
statutes.notes: Confirm current Act number after revision.

statutes.title: Interpretation Acts 1948 and 1967
statutes.notes: Essential for the statutory interpretation module.

statutes.title: Civil Law Act 1956
statutes.notes: Governs the reception of English common law and equity into Malaysia.

statutes.title: Courts of Judicature Act 1964
statutes.notes: Superior court jurisdiction. Pair with the Subordinate Courts Act 1948.

modules.title: Administrative Law
modules.gap: No current Malaysian student text identified. Read Malaysian judicial review judgments directly.

vendors.name: Joshua Legal Art Gallery
vendors.notes: Specialist law bookseller. Free shipping in Malaysia and Singapore. Stocks student editions.

vendors.name: Marsden Law Book
vendors.notes: Specialist law bookseller. Good for current editions and student editions.

vendors.name: Kinokuniya Malaysia
vendors.notes: General bookstore with a law section.

vendors.name: MPH Online
vendors.notes: Stocks Our Constitution and similar general-reader titles.

vendors.name: AGC — Laws of Malaysia portal
vendors.notes: All federal statutes as PDF. The only official publication of the laws of Malaysia, but a print-out is NOT a copy of the Gazette and does not constitute prima facie evidence.

purchasingNotes: Always ask for the STUDENT EDITION — same content, typically far cheaper than the practitioner edition.
Download every statute free from lom.agc.gov.my before buying any textbook.
Several standard Malaysian student texts are 5-20 years old. Pair every textbook with the current statute text.

Free sources have no citator: you cannot confirm from lom.agc.gov.my or CommonLII alone that a case is still good law. Budget for CLJ/LexisNexis access, or use Westlaw Asia if you obtain Bar-member access.
Verify every entry marked 'unconfirmed' with the bookseller before paying.
